subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should session-memory indexing be changed to preserve unchanged chunks on current main, and if so should maintainers sponsor a fresh implementation or rescue the conflicting open PR?
rationale: The fix shape affects session-state correctness, SQLite schema behavior, source-wide batching, compaction fallback, and whether the stale candidate branch is worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema and source-wide batching paths with focused compaction and overlap tests.

options.title: Rescue the open PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete assumptions before another review cycle.

options.title: Keep full-entry reindexing
options.body: Leave the existing full-file rewrite behavior if maintainers decide consistency is worth the extra long-session indexing cost.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema and source-wide batching paths with focused compaction and overlap tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent storage/schema history makes this the best available owner for the schema-sensitive decision.
